brief.summary_1line: Rama hears the monkeys’ doubts about Vibhishana but declares that anyone seeking refuge—even an enemy—must be granted protection.

image_candidates.scene_text: Rama stands calmly among the gathered monkey chiefs as they argue, while the distant figure of Vibhishana waits in the sky seeking refuge.
Rama raises his hand in assurance, declaring protection for anyone who comes saying 'I am yours.'
A lone pigeon offers its own flesh to a hawk that had taken refuge with it, illustrating Rama’s story of ultimate hospitality.

deep.rich_summary: As Vibhishana, brother of Ravana, seeks refuge with Rama, the monkey leaders debate whether he should be trusted. Some argue that abandoning one’s own brother in crisis proves treachery and that the demon may be a spy sent by Ravana. Rama listens carefully but explains that political realities often divide royal families and that motives—such as ambition or disgust with Ravana’s cruelty—could explain Vibhishana’s defection. More importantly, Rama declares a moral principle greater than strategy: anyone who approaches him seeking refuge must be protected, even if he were an enemy. Citing sacred teachings and the story of a pigeon who sacrificed itself to shelter a foe, Rama affirms the dharma of sanctuary, revealing both his confidence in his power and the ethical foundation of his kingship.

highlight_spans.why: Early counsel analyzing Vibhishana’s character and the difficulty of judging strangers establishes the political and moral dilemma.
Rama’s declaration that he will never refuse one who comes as a friend introduces the central ethical stance of the chapter.
Rama’s reflection on how kings often face betrayal from relatives and neighbors frames Vibhishana’s defection within royal politics.
The parable of the hospitable pigeon who offers his own flesh to a foe dramatizes the ideal of sacred hospitality.
Rama’s vow that anyone who seeks refuge with him will be protected is one of the most famous ethical statements in the epic.

top_scenes.scene_text: Rama standing calmly among the gathered monkey chiefs as they debate fiercely about the fate of the demon Vibhishana waiting in the sky for judgment.
Rama raising his hand in solemn vow, declaring protection for any being who seeks refuge, while the monkey army watches in awe.
The symbolic tale of a humble pigeon offering its own flesh to feed a hawk that had taken shelter with it, illustrating sacred hospitality.
